SEARCH
Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.search

Class SearchEngine

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.search.SearchEngine
public final class SearchEngine extends Object
The advanced-search engine: walks one or more directory roots in parallel, applies the query's name / kind / size / recency / content filters, grades each hit for relevance and streams matches to a consumer the moment they are found.

Design goals, in order:

  • Robust — unreadable directories, permission errors, dangling symlinks and vanished files are skipped, never thrown; symlinked folders are not descended into, so symlink loops cannot hang the walk; an invalid glob/regex matches nothing instead of crashing.
  • Performant — a fixed pool of daemon workers sized to the CPU count traverses breadth-first; patterns are compiled once; the walk stops early at the result cap; content grepping skips binaries and huge files.
  • Live — results are delivered incrementally (under a lock, so the consumer sees a serialised stream it can marshal to the EDT) and the returned SearchHandle cancels or awaits completion.

The engine holds no mutable state between searches, so a single instance may run many concurrent searches.

  • Method Details

    • getParallelism

      public int getParallelism()
      The worker count this engine uses.

    • search

      public SearchHandle search(SearchQuery query, Consumer<SearchMatch> sink)
      Runs query asynchronously, streaming each match to sink. The sink is invoked from worker threads under a lock (serialised, never concurrently); a UI consumer should marshal to its own thread. The returned SearchHandle cancels the walk and reports completion.

      A null query, a null sink, or a query with no roots yields an already-finished handle and emits nothing.

    • search

      public SearchHandle search(SearchQuery query, Consumer<SearchMatch> sink, Runnable onDone)
      As search(SearchQuery, Consumer) but additionally runs onDone exactly once when the walk finishes (completed, capped or cancelled), on whichever worker observes completion.

    • searchAll

      public List<SearchMatch> searchAll(SearchQuery query) throws InterruptedException
      Convenience: runs query to completion on background workers, blocking the caller, and returns the matches sorted by descending relevance (ties broken by path). Intended for tests and simple one-shot callers; a UI should prefer the streaming search(org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.search.SearchQuery, java.util.function.Consumer<org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.search.SearchMatch>) so results appear live.
      Throws:
      InterruptedException - if the calling thread is interrupted while waiting
